findings.title: §1 Purpose item 2 unconditionally describes the per-adopter onboarding contract as always including an invocation-log entry — contradicts invariant 2 for blocked-on-adopter-conflict close-state
findings.evidence:
**§1 Purpose item 2 (plan-doc line 30)** reads:

'2. Defines a **per-adopter onboarding contract** that each cascade slice satisfies: (a) caller wrapper PR'd into the adopter repo with SCP federation primitive SHA-pinned per VERSIONING.md (D-036); **(b) `scripts/enable-required-check.sh` invocation per D-035 with invocation-log entry under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`**; (c) post-bake observation window of ≥1 calendar week before cascade declares the adopter onboarded; (d) opt-in scorecard-emit ...'

Item (b) is stated unconditionally. The description 'that each cascade slice satisfies' makes this apply to all cascade slices with no carve-out.

This is the identical defect class as R4-NEW-MAJ-002, which was found and fixed at §3. The fix-round-4 edit correctly applied the conditional carve-out to §3 and §5.2 line 122, but did not propagate to §1 — the highest-level reader entry-point for the plan-doc. A first-time reader of §1 (the Purpose summary, universally read first) forms the model that ALL cascade slices ship (a) wrapper + (b) invocation-log entry + (c) post-bake window. When implementing a `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` cascade slice, such a reader would include a log entry in the PR. This would trigger the CI negative-assertion failure in `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` that invariant 2 is specifically designed to catch (invariant 2 line 47: 'PR MUST NOT modify `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`' for that close-state).

The inconsistency is directly verifiable: §1 item 2(b) says 'invocation-log entry' unconditionally; §3 line 73 now says 'only when `cascade-status` is `onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`'; §5.2 line 122 says 'only when `cascade-status: onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`'; invariant 2 line 47 says 'PR MUST NOT modify ... (no `enable-required-check.sh` invocation occurred)'. Three of the four loci were updated by fix-round-3 / fix-round-4; §1 Purpose item 2 was not.

This is the same propagation gap pattern identified in FIX-ROUND-4.md ('when adding a carve-out clause, enumerate the full set of states ... fix-round-3's edit added the negative assertion for one path but didn't propagate it through R-024-06 or §3'). This round's fix correctly propagated to §3 but missed §1.
findings.recommendation:
Update §1 Purpose item 2(b) to add the same conditional carve-out applied to §3 at fix-round-4. Replace:

'(b) `scripts/enable-required-check.sh` invocation per D-035 with invocation-log entry under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`'

with:

'(b) `scripts/enable-required-check.sh` invocation per D-035 with invocation-log entry under `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md` — **only when `cascade-status: onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`**; conflict-close (`blocked-on-adopter-conflict`) slices ship no log entry (CI asserts log NOT modified per invariant 2)'

This makes §1 consistent with §3, §5.2 line 122, and invariant 2 — all four loci in the model that determine how a cascade-slice executor understands the log-entry requirement.

findings.title: DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 4 says 'invariant 2 makes log-entry mandatory' — now incorrect after fix-round-3 introduced the three-path conditional model
findings.evidence:
**DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 4 (DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 69)** reads:

'4. **Estate-wide branch-protection mass-mutation risk.** Cascade slices invoke `enable-required-check.sh` — a mishap here mass-mutates the estate. Mitigation: D-035's CI-refusal + invocation log + **invariant 2 makes log-entry mandatory**. Plan-doc surfaces this as T-024-01 + T-024-02.'

The phrase 'invariant 2 makes log-entry mandatory' was accurate prior to fix-round-3, when invariant 2 specified that all cascade slices must include a log entry. After fix-round-3 added the `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` carve-out and fix-round-4 formally closed the three-value model, invariant 2 does NOT make log-entry unconditionally mandatory:

- For `onboarded` and `onboarded-operator-bump`: log entry required (mandatory).
- For `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`: log entry FORBIDDEN; CI asserts absence.

The description 'invariant 2 makes log-entry mandatory' now mischaracterizes invariant 2's semantics. A reader of the DISPATCH-NOTE risk section would form the incorrect model that invariant 2 mandates a log entry for every cascade slice — the same misconception that R4-NEW-MAJ-002 identified as producing implementors who add log entries to conflict-close slices.

The DISPATCH-NOTE is a planning artefact included in the plan package reviewed at each fix-round. The 024A DISPATCH-NOTE risk section is a normative description of the design's safety properties. Mischaracterizing invariant 2 in the risk narrative creates an inconsistency between the plan-doc invariant 2 (which is correct) and the DISPATCH-NOTE's characterization of that invariant (which describes the old, pre-fix-round-3 model). This is the same propagation class as R4-NEW-MAJ-001 (R-024-06 described the old weaker CI check behavior after invariant 2 was strengthened).

Note: DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) (line 51) also uses the label 'operator-run + invocation-logged' as the name for invariant 2 without qualification. However that is a checklist navigator label, not a normative statement about what cascade slices must ship, so it is a nit rather than a MAJ. The risk item 4 statement is the MAJ because it explicitly claims a behavioural property of invariant 2 ('makes log-entry mandatory') that is now false.
findings.recommendation:
Update DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 4 to accurately describe invariant 2's current semantics. Replace:

'Mitigation: D-035's CI-refusal + invocation log + invariant 2 makes log-entry mandatory.'

with:

'Mitigation: D-035's CI-refusal + invocation log + invariant 2 applies a conditional check-path — log entry required for `onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` close-states; log entry FORBIDDEN (and CI-asserted absent) for `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` close-state. Unlogged invocations against the wrong adopter are forensically detectable via absence of expected log entries.'

Also update DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) label from 'operator-run + invocation-logged' to 'operator-run + conditionally-invocation-logged (per cascade-status)' to remove the nit-level inconsistency with the three-path model.

findings.title: §4 threat model rows T-024-01 through T-024-10 — no remaining propagation gaps found
findings.evidence:
Each threat model row was reviewed for references to old unconditional log-entry behavior or old two-value cascade-status model:

- T-024-01 (wrong-adopter misfire): references invocation log in the capture-before context; accurate.
- T-024-02 (compromised credentials): 'forensically detectable via the absence of invocation log entries' — refers to the case where a malicious invocation occurred WITHOUT a log entry, not to conflict-close slices. Accurate for its intended threat (credential-compromise scenario assumes an invocation happened); does not describe the carve-out for conflict-close (where no invocation occurred). Not a defect.
- T-024-03 (adopter-side rejection): 'cascade slice itself is still mergeable on the SCP repo because it ships only docs + invocation log entries' — this row describes the path where the invocation HAD already happened before the adopter rejected the wrapper PR (post-invocation rejection, not pre-invocation conflict discovery). This is accurately distinct from `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` (pre-invocation). Not a defect.
- T-024-04 through T-024-10: no references to invocation log entries or cascade-status close-states. No propagation gaps found.

Conclusion: §4 threat model is clean for propagation gaps on the cascade-status / CI-enforcement spec.

findings.title: DISPATCH-NOTE slice acceptance checklist criteria — cascade-status spec coverage assessment
findings.evidence:
The 14 DISPATCH-NOTE slice acceptance checklist criteria (items i–xiv) were reviewed for missing cascade-status spec references:

- Criterion (iii) describes invariant 2 as 'operator-run + invocation-logged' — a summary label that does not capture the three-path conditional. This is a nit (checklist navigator label, not normative prose); the normative spec is in the plan-doc §2 invariant 2. Not MAJ.
- Criterion (iv) through (xiv): none reference cascade-status or the CI-enforcement spec in a way that would mislead an implementor.
- No checklist criterion contains a normative claim that all cascade slices ship a log entry.

Conclusion: DISPATCH-NOTE checklist criteria contain one nit (criterion iii label) captured in the recommendation for R5-NEW-MAJ-002, but no additional MAJ-level gaps beyond R5-NEW-MAJ-002.
